plain_english_summary: While the investigation is ongoing, a victim can request the company to transfer her or the accused, or grant her up to 3 months of paid leave (which does not consume her regular leave balance) to ensure her safety and comfort.

title: Inquiry report
text: On the completion of an inquiry under this Act, the Internal Committee or the Local Committee, as the case may be, shall provide a report of its findings to the employer... within a period of ten days from the date of completion of the inquiry... [cite: 201]

sub_structure.2: Where the... Committee... arrives at the conclusion that the allegation against the respondent has not been proved, it shall recommend to the employer... that no action is required to be taken in the matter. [cite: 202]
sub_structure.3_i: to take action for sexual harassment as a misconduct in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable... [cite: 204, 205]
sub_structure.3_ii: to deduct, notwithstanding anything in the service rules applicable... from the salary or wages of the respondent such sum as it may consider appropriate to be paid to the aggrieved woman... [cite: 204, 206]
sub_structure.4: The employer or the District Officer shall act upon the recommendation within sixty days of its receipt by him. [cite: 209]

plain_english_summary: After the 90-day inquiry, the committee has 10 days to submit a report. If the accused is found guilty, the committee can recommend taking disciplinary action and deducting compensation directly from the accused's salary. The employer must enforce this within 60 days.

title: Punishment for false or malicious complaint and false evidence
text: Where the... Committee... arrives at a conclusion that the allegation against the respondent is malicious or the aggrieved woman... has made the complaint knowing it to be false or... has produced any forged or misleading document, it may recommend to the employer... to take action against the woman or the person who has made the complaint... [cite: 210, 211]

sub_structure.1_proviso_1: Provided that a mere inability to substantiate a complaint or provide adequate proof need not attract action against the complainant under this section: [cite: 212]
sub_structure.1_proviso_2: Provided further that the malicious intent on part of the complainant shall be established after an inquiry... before any action is recommended. [cite: 213]
sub_structure.2: Where the... Committee... arrives at a conclusion that during the inquiry any witness has given false evidence... it may recommend to the employer... to take action... [cite: 214]

plain_english_summary: If the committee proves that a complaint was intentionally false or malicious, or if a witness lied, the company can punish the liar. However, simply failing to prove an allegation due to lack of evidence does not mean the complaint was false or malicious.

title: Determination of compensation
text: For the purpose of determining the sums to be paid to the aggrieved woman under clause (ii) of sub-section (3) of section 13, the Internal Committee or the Local Committee, as the case may be, shall have regard to- [cite: 215]

sub_structure.a: the mental trauma, pain, suffering and emotional distress caused to the aggrieved woman; [cite: 216]
sub_structure.b: the loss in the career opportunity due to the incident of sexual harassment; [cite: 217]
sub_structure.c: medical expenses incurred by the victim for physical or psychiatric treatment; [cite: 218]
sub_structure.d: the income and financial status of the respondent; [cite: 219]
sub_structure.e: feasibility of such payment in lump sum or in instalments. [cite: 220]

plain_english_summary: When deciding how much money the harasser must pay the victim, the committee must look at the victim's trauma, medical bills, lost career opportunities, and the harasser's financial ability to pay.

title: Prohibition of publication or making known contents of complaint and inquiry proceedings
text: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Right to Information Act, 2005 (22 of 2005), the contents of the complaint made under section 9, the identity and addresses of the aggrieved woman, respondent and witnesses, any information relating to conciliation and inquiry proceedings... shall not be published, communicated or made known to the public, press and media in any manner: [cite: 222, 223]

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that information may be disseminated regarding the justice secured to any vicitim of sexual harassment under this Act without disclosing the name, address, identity or any other particulars calculated to lead to the identification of the aggrieved woman and witnesses. [cite: 224]

plain_english_summary: POSH proceedings are strictly confidential. No one can leak the identities of the victim, accused, or witnesses, nor can they share the contents of the complaint with the media or public. Companies can only announce that justice was served without revealing identifying details.

title: Penalty for publication or making known contents of complaint and inquiry proceedings
text: Where any person entrusted with the duty to handle or deal with the complaint, inquiry or any recommendations or action to be taken under the provisions of this Act, contravenes the provisions of section 16, he shall be liable for penalty in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable to the said person or where no such service rules exist, in such manner as may be prescribed. [cite: 225]
plain_english_summary: If any committee member, HR personnel, or company official leaks confidential information regarding a sexual harassment case, they will be penalized under the company's service rules.

title: Appeal
text: Any person aggrieved from the recommendations made under sub-section (2) of section 13 or under clause (i) or clause (ii) of sub-section (3) of section 13 or sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) of section 14 or section 17 or non-implementation of such recommendations may prefer an appeal to the court or tribunal in accordance with the provisions of the service rules applicable... [cite: 226, 227]

sub_structure.2: The appeal under sub-section (1) shall be preferred within a period of ninety days of the recommendations. [cite: 228]

plain_english_summary: If either the victim or the accused is unhappy with the committee's final decision, or if the employer fails to implement the decision, they have 90 days to file an appeal with a court or tribunal.

title: Duties of employer
text: Every employer shall- (a) provide a safe working environment at the workplace with shall include safety from the persons coming into contact at the workplace; [cite: 231, 232]

sub_structure.b: display at any conspicuous place in the workplace, the penal consequences of sexual harassments; and the order constituting, the Internal Committee... [cite: 233, 234]
sub_structure.c: organise workshops and awareness programmes at regular intervals for sensitising the employees... [cite: 235]
sub_structure.d: provide necessary facilities to the Internal Committee... for dealing with the complaint and conducting an inquiry; [cite: 236]
sub_structure.g: provide assistance to the woman if she so chooses to file a complaint in relation to the offence under the Indian Penal Code... [cite: 239]
sub_structure.i: treat sexual harassment as a misconduct under the service rules and initiate action for such misconduct; [cite: 242]

plain_english_summary: Startups and employers have a strict legal duty to provide a safe workplace. They must display the names of the ICC members in the office, conduct regular anti-harassment training for employees, officially label sexual harassment as 'misconduct' in the employee handbook, and help victims file a police complaint if requested.

chapter_title: DUTIES AND POWERS OF DISTRICT OFFICER
title: Duties and powers of District Officer
text: The District Officer shall, (a) monitor the timely submission of report furnished by the Local Committee; [cite: 246, 247]

sub_structure.b: take such measures as may be necessary for engaging non-governmental organisations for creation of awareness on sexual harassment and the rights of the women. [cite: 248]

plain_english_summary: The government's appointed District Officer is responsible for making sure the Local Committees submit their reports on time and working with NGOs to raise awareness about women's rights regarding workplace harassment.

title: Committee to submit annual report
text: The Internal Committee or the Local Committee, as the case may be, shall in each calendar year prepare, in such form and at such time as may be prescribed, an annual report and submit the same to the employer and the District Officer. [cite: 250]

sub_structure.2: The District Officer shall forward a brief report on the annual reports received under sub-section (1) to the State Government. [cite: 251]

plain_english_summary: Every year, the company's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) must prepare an annual report detailing its activities and submit it to both the employer (the startup) and the government's District Officer.

title: Employer to include information in annual report
text: The employer shall include in its report the number of cases filed, if any, and their disposal under this Act in the annual report of his organisation or where no such report is required to be prepared, intimate such number of cases, if any, to the District Officer. [cite: 252]
plain_english_summary: Startups must publicly declare the number of sexual harassment cases filed and resolved in their company's official annual report. If the startup isn't legally required to publish an annual report, they must send these numbers directly to the District Officer.

title: Appropriate Government to monitor implementation and maintain data
text: The appropriate Government shall monitor the implementation of this Act and maintain date on the number of cases filed and disposed of in respect of all cases of sexual harassment at workplace. [cite: 253]
plain_english_summary: The government is required to actively track how well this law is being followed and keep a centralized database of how many workplace harassment cases are filed and resolved.

title: Appropriate Government to take measures to publicise the Act
text: The appropriate Government may, subject to the availability of financial and other resources,- [cite: 254, 255]

sub_structure.a: develop relevant information, education, communication and training materials, and organise awareness programmes, to advance the understanding of the public of the provisions of this Act... [cite: 256]
sub_structure.b: formulate orientation and training programmes for the members of the [Local Committee]. [cite: 257]

plain_english_summary: The government is responsible for creating educational materials and running awareness campaigns to help the public understand the POSH Act, as well as training the members of the Local Committees.

title: Power to call for information and inspection of records
text: The appropriate Government, on being satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest or in the interest of women employees at a workplace to do so, by order in writing,- [cite: 259]

sub_structure.1_a: call upon any employer or District Officer to furnish in writing such information relating to sexual harassment as it may require; [cite: 260]
sub_structure.1_b: authorise any officer to make inspection of the records and workplace in relation to sexual harassment, who shall submit a report of such inspection... [cite: 261]
sub_structure.2: Every employer and District Officer shall produce on demand before the officer making the inspection all information, records and other documents in his custody... [cite: 262]

plain_english_summary: The government has the right to demand written information about sexual harassment issues from a startup and can send an officer to inspect the startup's workplace and internal records. The startup is legally obligated to hand over these documents during an inspection.

title: Penalty for non-compliance with provisions of Act
text: Where the employer fails to- (a) constitute an Internal Committee under sub-section (1) of section 4; [cite: 263]

sub_structure.1_b: take action under sections 13, 14 and 22; and [cite: 266]
sub_structure.1_c: contravenes or attempts to contravene or abets contravention of other provisions of this Act or any rules made thereunder, he shall be punishable with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees. [cite: 267, 268]
sub_structure.2_i: If any employer, after having been previously convicted of an offence punishable under this Act subsequently commits and is convicted of the same offence, he shall be liable to- twice the punishment, which might have been imposed on a first conviction... [cite: 269, 270]
sub_structure.2_ii: cancellation, of his licence or withdrawal, or non-renewal, or approval, or cancellation of the registration, as the case may be, by the Government or local authority required for carrying on his business or activity. [cite: 272]

plain_english_summary: If a startup fails to set up an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) or ignores the committee's recommendations, they can be fined up to 50,000 rupees. If they repeat the offense, the fine is doubled, and the government can legally cancel their business licenses and shut down their operations.

title: Cognizance of offence by courts
text: No court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act or any rules made thereunder, save on a complaint made by the aggrieved woman or any person authorised by the Internal Committee or Local Committee in this behalf. [cite: 273]

sub_structure.2: No court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act. [cite: 274]
sub_structure.3: Every offence under this Act shall be non-cognizable. [cite: 275]

plain_english_summary: A regular court will only hear a case about a POSH Act violation if the complaint is brought forward by the victim herself or someone officially authorized by the ICC. These offences are 'non-cognizable', meaning the police cannot make an arrest without a warrant.

title: Act not in derogation of any other law
text: The provisions of this Act shall be in addition to and not in derogation of the provisions of any other law for the time being in force. [cite: 276]
plain_english_summary: The POSH Act does not replace any other existing laws (like the Indian Penal Code). Its rules act as an additional layer of compliance and protection on top of whatever else is already legally required.

title: Power of appropriate Government to make rules
text: The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the provisions of this Act. [cite: 277]

sub_structure.2: In particular and without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, such rules may provide for all or any of the following matters... [cite: 278]
sub_structure.3: Every rule made by the Central Government under this Act shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament... [cite: 295]
sub_structure.4: Any rule made under sub-section (4) of section 8 by the State Government shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of the State Legislature... [cite: 298]

plain_english_summary: The Central Government is authorized to create specific, detailed rules (like forms and procedures) to carry out the broader principles of the POSH Act. These rules must be presented to and approved by Parliament.

title: Power to remove difficulties
text: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions, not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, as may appear to it to be necessary for removing the difficulty: [cite: 299]

sub_structure.1_proviso: Provided that no such order shall be made under this section after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act. [cite: 300]
sub_structure.2: Every order made under this section shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament. [cite: 301]

plain_english_summary: For the first two years after the Act passed, the Central Government had the special power to issue orders to quickly fix any practical difficulties that arose while implementing the new law.

title: Short title, extent and commencement
text: This Act may be called the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976.

sub_structure.2: It extends to the whole of India.
sub_structure.3: It shall come into force on such date, not being later than three years from the passing of this Act, as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different establishments or employments.

plain_english_summary: This section outlines the name of the Act and establishes that it applies to the entirety of India.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires.-

sub_structure.c: "employer" has the meaning assigned to it in clause (f) of section 2 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 (39 of 1972);
sub_structure.g: "remuneration" means the basic wage or salary, and any additional emoluments whatsoever payable, either in cash or in kind, to a person employed in respect of employment or work done in such employment, if the terms of the contract of employment, express or implied, were fulfilled;
sub_structure.h: "same work or work of a similar nature" means work in respect of which the skill, effort and responsibility required are the same, when performed under similar working conditions, by a man or a woman and the differences, if any, between the skill, effort and responsibility required of a man and those required of a woman are not of practical importance in relation to the terms and conditions of employment;

plain_english_summary: Defines key terms for startups. 'Remuneration' includes basic salary plus any additional cash or in-kind perks. 'Same work or work of a similar nature' means jobs requiring the same skill, effort, and responsibility under similar conditions, regardless of minor differences.

title: Act to have over riding effect
text: The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law or in the terms of any award, agreement or contract of service, whether made before or after the commencement of this Act, or in any instrument having effect under any law for the time being in force.
plain_english_summary: The rules of this Act override any other conflicting laws, employment contracts, or company agreements. A startup cannot use an employment contract to bypass the requirement for equal pay.

chapter_title: PAYMENT OF REMUNERATION AT EQUAL RATES TO MEN AND WOMEN WORKERS AND OTHER MATTERS
title: Duty of employer to pay equal remuneration to men and women workers for same work or work of a similar nature
text: No employer shall pay to any worker, employed by him in an establishment or employment, remuneration, whether payable in cash or in kind, at rates less favourable than those at which remuneration is paid by him to the workers of the opposite sex in such establishment or employment for performing the same work or work of a similar nature.

sub_structure.2: No employer shall, for the purpose of complying with the provisions of sub-section (1), reduce the rate of remuneration of any worker.
sub_structure.3: Where, in an establishment or employment, the rates of remuneration payable before the commencement of this Act for men and women workers for the same work or work of a similar nature are different only on the ground of sex, then the higher... or, as the case may be, the highest... of such rates shall be the rate at which remuneration shall be payable...

plain_english_summary: Employers are legally obligated to pay men and women equally for the same or similar work. To fix a pay gap, a startup cannot lower anyone's salary; instead, they must raise the lower-paid employee's salary to match the higher rate.

chapter_title: PAYMENT OF REMUNERATION AT EQUAL RATES TO MEN AND WOMEN WORKERS AND OTHER MATTERS
title: No discrimination to be made while recruiting men and women workers
text: On and from the commencement of this Act, no employer shall while making recruitment for the same work or work of a similar nature, or in any condition of service subsequent to recruitment such as promotions, training or transfer, make any discrimination against women except where the employment of women in such work is prohibited or restricted by or under any law for the time being in force:

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that the provisions of this section shall not affect any priority or reservation for Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, ex-servicemen, retrenched employees or any other class or category of persons in the matter of recruitment to the posts in an establishment or employment.

plain_english_summary: Startups are strictly prohibited from discriminating against women during hiring, promotions, training opportunities, or transfers, unless a specific law restricts women from doing that exact type of work. Standard legal reservations (like SC/ST) still apply.

chapter_title: PAYMENT OF REMUNERATION AT EQUAL RATES TO MEN AND WOMEN WORKERS AND OTHER MATTERS
title: Advisory Committee
text: For the purpose of providing increasing employment opportunities for women, the appropriate Government shall constitute one or more Advisory Committees to advise it with regard to the extent to which women may be employed in such establishments or employments as the Central Government may, by notification, specify in this behalf.

sub_structure.2: Every Advisory Committee shall consist of not less than ten persons, to be nominated by the appropriate Government, of which one-half shall be women.
sub_structure.5: The appropriate Government may, after considering the advice tendered to it by the Advisory Committee... issue such directions in respect of employment of women workers, as the appropriate Government may think fit.

plain_english_summary: The government will form Advisory Committees (with at least 50% women members) to figure out how to increase employment opportunities for women. The government can issue binding directions to companies based on this advice.

chapter_title: PAYMENT OF REMUNERATION AT EQUAL RATES TO MEN AND WOMEN WORKERS AND OTHER MATTERS
title: Power of appropriate Government to appoint authorities for hearing and deciding claims and complaints
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint such officers, not below the rank of a Labour Officer, as it thinks fit to be the authorities for the purpose of hearing and deciding- (a) Complaints with regard to the contravention of any provision of this Act; (b) claims arising out of non-payment of wages at equal rates to men and women workers for the same work or work of a similar nature...

sub_structure.4_i: in the case of a claim arising out of non-payment of wages at equal rates... that payment he made to the worker of the amount by which the wages payable to him exceed the amount actually paid;
sub_structure.5: Every authority appointed under sub-section (1) shall have all the powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908... for the purpose of taking evidence and of enforcing the attendance of witnesses and compelling the production of documents...
sub_structure.6: Any employer or worker aggrieved by any order made by an authority appointed under sub-section (1), on a complaint or claim may, within thirty days from the date of the order, prefer an appeal to such authority as the appropriate Government may... specify...

plain_english_summary: The government will appoint authorities to hear complaints about unequal pay or discrimination. These authorities have civil court powers and can legally order a startup to pay the missing wage difference to the underpaid employee. These rulings can be appealed within 30 days.

title: Duty of employers to maintain registers
text: On and from the commencement of this Act, every employer shall maintain such registers and other documents in relation to the workers employed by him as may be prescribed.
plain_english_summary: Startups and employers must maintain specific legal registers and paperwork regarding their employees to prove they are complying with the equal pay laws.

title: Inspectors
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint such persons as it may think fit to be Inspectors for the purpose of making an investigation as to whether the provisions of this Act, or the rules made thereunder, are being complied with by employers...

sub_structure.3_a: enter, at any reasonable time, with such assistance as he thinks fit, any building, factory, premises or vessel;
sub_structure.3_b: require any employer to produce any register, muster-roll or other documents relating to the employment of workers, and examine such documents;
sub_structure.3_d: examine the employer, his agent or servant or any other person found in charge of the establishment...
sub_structure.4: Any person required by an Inspector to produce any register or other document or to give any information shall comply with such requisition.

plain_english_summary: The government appoints Inspectors who have the legal right to enter a startup's premises at any reasonable time, demand to see employee registers, and interrogate the founders or managers to ensure they are paying men and women equally.

title: Penalties
text: If after the commencement of this Act, any employer, being required by or under the Act, so to do- (a) omits or fails to maintain any register or other document in relation to workers employed by him... he shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month or with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees or with both.

sub_structure.1_b: omits or fails to produce any register, muster-roll or other document relating to the employment of workers, or
sub_structure.1_c: omits or refuses to give any evidence or prevents his agent... from giving evidence, or
sub_structure.2: If, after the commencement of this Act, any employer- (a) makes any recruitment in contravention of the provisions of this Act, or (b) makes any payment of remuneration at unequal rates... or (c) makes any discrimination... he shall be punishable with fine which shall not be less than ten thousand rupees but which may extend to twenty thousand rupees or with imprisonment for a term which shall be not less than three months but which may extend to one year or with both...

plain_english_summary: Startups face strict criminal penalties for non-compliance. Failing to keep records or cooperating with inspectors can lead to a 10,000 rupee fine and a month in jail. Actually paying unequal wages or discriminating in hiring leads to fines between 10,000 and 20,000 rupees, and between three months to a year in jail for the first offense.

title: Short title, extent and commencement
text: (1) This Act may be called the Designs Act, 2000.

sub_structure.2: (2) It extends to the whole of India.
sub_structure.3: (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the official name of the Act, confirms it applies across India, and notes that different sections could be brought into force on different dates by government notification.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context.

sub_structure.a: (a) "article" means any article of manufacture and any substance, artificial, or partly artificial and partly natural and includes any part of an article capable of being made and sold separately;
sub_structure.b: (b) "Controller" means the Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks referred to in Section 3;
sub_structure.c: (c) "copyright" means the exclusive right to apply a design to any article in any class in which the design is registered;
sub_structure.d: (d) "design" means only the features of shape, configuration, pattern, ornament or composition of lines or colours applied to any article whether in two dimensional or three dimensional or in both forms, by any industrial process or means... but does not include any mode or principle of construction or anything which is in substance a mere mechanical device, and does not include any trade mark... property mark... or any artistic work as defined in clause (c) of section 2 of the Copyright Act, 1957;
sub_structure.g: (g) "original", in relation to a design, means originating from the author of such design and includes the cases which though old in themselves yet are new in their application;
sub_structure.j: (j) "proprietor of a new or original design" means, depending on the circumstances, the person for whom the design was executed for consideration, the person who acquired the design or the right to apply it, or the author of the design.

plain_english_summary: Defines the key terms of the Act. Most important for software/product teams: 'design' is limited to features of shape, pattern, or ornamentation judged solely by the eye, and explicitly excludes anything that is in substance a mechanical device or that overlaps with copyright/trademark protection — so purely functional UI logic or code cannot be protected as a 'design' under this Act, only the visual/ornamental appearance of a physical or graphical article.

title: Controller and other officers
text: (1) The Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks appointed under sub-section (1) of section 4 of the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958 shall be the Controller of Designs for the purposes of this Act.

sub_structure.2: (2) For the purposes of this Act, the Central Government may appoint as many examiners and other officers and with such designations, as it thinks fit.
sub_structure.3: (3) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the officers appointed under sub-section (2) shall discharge under the superintendence and directions of the Controller such functions of the Controller under this Act as he may, from time to time by general or special order in writing, authorise them to discharge.
sub_structure.4: (4) The Controller may by order in writing withdraw any matter pending before an officer appointed under sub-section (2) and deal with such matter himself or transfer it to another officer appointed under sub-section (2).

plain_english_summary: The same official who heads the Patents and Trade Marks offices also serves as the Controller of Designs, who can appoint examiners and delegate or withdraw pending matters.

title: Prohibition of registration of certain designs
text: A design which- (a) is not new or original; or (b) has been disclosed to the public anywhere in India or in any other country by publication in tangible form or by use or in any other way prior to the filing date, or where applicable, the priority date of the application for registration; or (c) is not significantly distinguishable from known designs or combination of known designs; or (d) comprises or contains scandalous or obscene matter shall not be registered.
plain_english_summary: A design cannot be registered if it isn't new/original, was already publicly disclosed anywhere before filing, is too similar to existing designs, or contains scandalous/obscene content — comparable to the novelty and prior-art bars in patent law.

title: Application for registration of designs
text: (1) The Controller may, on the application of any person claiming to be the proprietor of any new or original design not previously published in any country and which is not contrary to public order or morality, register the design under this Act.

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that the Controller shall before such registration refer the application for examination, by an examiner appointed under sub-section (2) of section 3, as to whether such design is capable of being registered.
sub_structure.2: (2) Every application shall be in the prescribed form and filed in the Patent Office in the prescribed manner and accompanied by the prescribed fee.
sub_structure.3: (3) A design may be registered in not more than one class.
sub_structure.4: (4) The Controller may refuse to register any design; any person aggrieved by such refusal may appeal to the High Court.
sub_structure.5: (5) An application not completed within the prescribed time owing to default or neglect of the applicant shall be deemed abandoned.
sub_structure.6: (6) A design when registered shall be registered as of the date of the application for registration.

plain_english_summary: Sets out the registration process: applicants file a prescribed form and fee, the application is examined for registrability, refusals can be appealed to the High Court, and an incomplete application is treated as abandoned. The registration date is backdated to the filing date.

title: Registration to be in respect of particular article
text: (1) A design may be registered in respect of any or all of the articles comprised in a prescribed class of articles.

sub_structure.2: (2) Any question as to the class within which any article falls shall be determined by the Controller, whose decision shall be final.
sub_structure.3: (3) Registering a design for further articles in the same class shall not be refused, nor shall the earlier registration be invalidated, merely because the design was previously registered or published for another article in that class.
sub_structure.4: (4) If a person applies to register a design already registered by another person (or a variation not sufficiently different), and later becomes the registered proprietor of the earlier design while the application is pending, the earlier provisions apply as if the applicant had always owned that design.

plain_english_summary: Design registration is tied to a specific class of articles; you can extend registration of the same design to other articles within that class without losing or invalidating the original registration.

title: Publication of particulars of registered designs
text: The Controller shall, as soon as may be after the registration of a design, cause publication of the prescribed particulars of the design to be published in such manner as may be prescribed and thereafter the design shall be open to public inspection.
plain_english_summary: Once registered, a design's details are published and become publicly inspectable.

title: Power of Controller to make orders regarding substitution of applicant, etc.
text: (1) If the Controller is satisfied that, by virtue of an assignment or agreement in writing or by operation of law, a claimant would be entitled to a pending design application (or an interest in it) if the design were registered, the Controller may direct that the application proceed in the name of the claimant, in addition to or instead of the original applicant.

sub_structure.2: (2) No such direction shall be given by virtue of an assignment or agreement made by one of several joint applicants without the consent of the other joint applicants.
sub_structure.3: (3) No such direction shall be given unless the design is identified in the assignment, or an acknowledgment is produced, or the claimant's rights have been finally established by a court, or the Controller otherwise directs.
sub_structure.4: (4) If a joint applicant dies before registration, the Controller may, on request of the survivors and with consent of the deceased's legal representative, direct that the application proceed in the name of the survivors alone.
sub_structure.5: (5) If joint applicants dispute how the application should proceed, the Controller may, after hearing all parties, give directions to resolve it.

plain_english_summary: Lets the Controller substitute or add applicants on a pending design application where ownership has changed by assignment, agreement, death, or court decision — relevant when a design is transferred or a founder/co-applicant exits before registration completes.

title: Certificate of registration
text: (1) The Controller shall grant a certificate of registration to the proprietor of the design when registered.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Controller may, in case of loss of the original certificate or in any other case he deems expedient, furnish one or more copies of the certificate.

plain_english_summary: A registered proprietor receives an official certificate of registration, and duplicate copies can be issued if the original is lost.

title: Register of designs
text: (1) There shall be kept at the Patent Office a book called the register of designs, wherein shall be entered the names and addresses of proprietors of registered designs, notifications of assignments and transmissions, and such other matter as may be prescribed; the register may be maintained wholly or partly on computer, floppies or diskettes, subject to prescribed safeguards.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where the register is maintained wholly or partly on computer, floppies or diskettes, any reference in this Act to an entry in the register is construed as a reference to the entry so maintained.
sub_structure.3: (3) The register of designs existing at the commencement of this Act is incorporated into the register under this Act.
sub_structure.4: (4) The register of designs is prima facie evidence of any matter directed or authorised by this Act to be entered in it.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the official Register of Designs, expressly allows it to be kept electronically, and treats its entries as prima facie (presumptive) evidence in legal proceedings.

title: Copyright on registration
text: (1) When a design is registered, the registered proprietor shall, subject to the provisions of this Act, have copyright in the design during ten years from the date of registration.

sub_structure.2: (2) If, before the expiration of the ten years, an application for extension is made to the Controller in the prescribed manner, the Controller shall, on payment of the prescribed fee, extend the period of copyright for a second period of five years from the expiration of the original ten years.

plain_english_summary: Design registration grants a 10-year exclusivity term, extendable once for a further 5 years (15 years total) on payment of the prescribed fee — far shorter than the 60-year term under the Copyright Act.

title: Restoration of lapsed designs
text: (1) Where a design has ceased to have effect due to failure to pay the extension fee under section 11(2), the proprietor (or, for jointly held designs, one or more proprietors with the Controller's leave) may, within one year of lapse, apply for restoration in the prescribed manner on payment of the prescribed fee.

sub_structure.2: (2) The application must contain a verified statement fully setting out the circumstances of the failure to pay, and the Controller may require further evidence.

plain_english_summary: A lapsed design (due to a missed extension-fee payment) can be revived within one year if the proprietor explains the circumstances and pays the required fee.

title: Procedure for disposal of applications for restoration of lapsed designs
text: (1) If, after hearing the applicant (where desired) or as the Controller thinks fit, the Controller is satisfied that the failure to pay the extension fee was unintentional and there was no undue delay in applying, the Controller shall, on payment of the unpaid fee plus the prescribed additional fee, restore the registration.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Controller may, as a condition of restoration, require that any outstanding entry required by the Act be made in the register.

plain_english_summary: Restoration is granted only if the missed payment was unintentional and the application wasn't unduly delayed, and may be conditioned on bringing the register up to date.

title: Rights of proprietor of lapsed design which has been restored
text: (1) Where registration is restored, the proprietor's rights are subject to prescribed provisions and any conditions the Controller imposes to protect or compensate persons who began using, or took definite steps to use, the design during the lapse period.

sub_structure.2: (2) No suit or proceeding may be commenced for piracy of the design or infringement of its copyright for acts committed between the date the registration lapsed and the date it was restored.

plain_english_summary: If a design is restored after lapsing, third parties who started using it during the gap get protection, and the proprietor cannot sue for any infringement that occurred during that lapse window — an important risk to flag for anyone who used a design believing it was unprotected.

title: Requirements before delivery on sale
text: (1) Before delivery on sale of any articles to which a registered design has been applied, the proprietor shall (a) furnish to the Controller the prescribed representations or specimens of the design if not already furnished — failing which the Controller may erase the proprietor's name from the register, ending the copyright; and (b) mark each such article with the prescribed mark, words or figures denoting registration — failing which the proprietor cannot recover penalties or damages for infringement unless proper marking steps were taken or the infringer had actual notice of the registration.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Central Government may, on representation from a trade or industry, dispense with or modify the marking requirements for a class of articles by rule.

plain_english_summary: Products bearing a registered design generally must be marked as registered; failing to mark them can forfeit the proprietor's ability to claim damages against infringers, unless notice was otherwise given.

title: Effect of disclosure on copyright
text: The disclosure of a design by the proprietor to any other person, in circumstances that would make it contrary to good faith for that person to use or publish the design, and the disclosure of a design in breach of good faith by any person other than the proprietor, and the acceptance of a first and confidential order for articles bearing a new textile design intended for registration, shall not be deemed a publication sufficient to invalidate the copyright, if registration is obtained subsequently.
plain_english_summary: Sharing a design in confidence (e.g. under an NDA, or to a manufacturer for a first confidential order) doesn't count as public disclosure that would destroy the design's registrability, provided the recipient breaches confidence rather than you disclosing it publicly.

title: Inspection of registered designs
text: (1) During the existence of copyright in a design, any person furnishing information enabling the Controller to identify the design and paying the prescribed fee may inspect the design in the prescribed manner.

sub_structure.2: (2) Any person may, on application and payment of the prescribed fee, obtain a certified copy of any registered design.

plain_english_summary: Anyone can inspect a registered design or obtain a certified copy of it, on payment of a fee, while its copyright subsists.

title: Information as to existence of copyright
text: On the request of any person furnishing information to identify the design, and on payment of the prescribed fee, the Controller shall inform such person whether registration still exists, in respect of which classes of articles, and the date of registration and the name and address of the registered proprietor.
plain_english_summary: The public can request confirmation from the Controller on whether a specific design's registration is still active, and get the proprietor's details — useful for freedom-to-operate checks before launching a product.

title: Cancellation of registration
text: (1) Any person interested may petition the Controller, at any time after registration, for cancellation of a registered design on the grounds that: (a) the design was previously registered in India; (b) it was published in India or elsewhere before the registration date; (c) the design is not new or original; (d) the design is not registrable under this Act; or (e) it is not a "design" as defined in section 2(d).

sub_structure.2: (2) An appeal lies to the High Court from any Controller order under this section, and the Controller may refer a petition directly to the High Court for decision.

plain_english_summary: Gives any interested party (e.g. a competitor) grounds and a procedure to challenge and cancel a registered design — mirroring revocation proceedings under patent law — with a right of appeal to the High Court.

title: Designs to bind Government
text: A registered design shall have to all intents the like effect as against the Government as it has against any person, and the provisions of Chapter XVII of the Patents Act, 1970 shall apply to registered designs as they apply to patents.
plain_english_summary: Registered designs are enforceable against the Government itself, on the same terms that apply to patents under the Patents Act's government-use chapter.

title: Provisions as to exhibitions
text: Exhibiting a design (or an article bearing it) at a notified industrial/other exhibition, or publishing a description of it during or after the exhibition, shall not prevent the design from being registered or invalidate its registration, provided: (a) the exhibitor gives the Controller prior notice in the prescribed form; and (b) the registration application is made within six months of first exhibiting or publishing the design.
plain_english_summary: A limited 'grace period' exhibition exception: showing a design at a government-notified exhibition doesn't destroy its novelty, as long as the Controller is notified in advance and the registration application follows within six months.

title: Piracy of registered design
text: (1) During the existence of copyright in any design, it shall not be lawful for any person, without the licence or written consent of the registered proprietor, to: (a) apply (or cause to be applied), for the purpose of sale, the design or a fraudulent/obvious imitation of it to any article in the class in which it is registered; (b) import for sale any such article bearing the design or an imitation of it; or (c) publish, expose, or cause to be published or exposed for sale, an article knowingly bearing the design or an imitation of it without the proprietor's consent.

sub_structure.2: (2) Any person who contravenes is liable, per contravention, either (a) to pay the registered proprietor a sum not exceeding twenty-five thousand rupees recoverable as a contract debt (capped at fifty thousand rupees total per design), or (b) if the proprietor elects to sue, to pay damages as awarded and be restrained by injunction; no such suit may be instituted below the court of a District Judge.
sub_structure.3: (3) In any suit under sub-section (2), any ground on which the registration could be cancelled under section 19 is available as a defence.
sub_structure.4: (4) Where such a cancellation ground is raised as a defence, the suit shall be transferred to the High Court for decision.
sub_structure.5: (5) When a court makes a decree under sub-section (2), it must send a copy to the Controller, who enters it in the register of designs.

plain_english_summary: The core infringement provision: unauthorized commercial application, import for sale, or sale of a product bearing a registered design (or an obvious imitation) is 'piracy'. Remedies are either a capped statutory sum (Rs 25,000 per act, Rs 50,000 total per design) or an infringement suit for damages and injunction, which must be filed in a District Court or higher and gets escalated to the High Court if design validity is contested.

title: Application of certain provisions of the Patents Act to designs
text: The provisions of the Patents Act, 1970 with regard to certificates of validity of a patent, and to the remedy in case of groundless threats of legal proceedings by a patentee, shall apply to registered designs in like manner, substituting references to copyright in a design for patent, proprietor of a design for patentee, and design for invention.
plain_english_summary: Imports two useful Patents Act protections into design law: (1) a court-issued certificate of validity that shields the proprietor from re-litigating validity, and (2) a remedy against a design owner who makes groundless infringement threats — relevant if a competitor sends an unfounded cease-and-desist.

title: Fees
text: (1) Such fees as may be prescribed shall be paid in respect of the registration of designs, applications therefor, and other matters relating to designs under this Act.

sub_structure.2: (2) A proceeding for which a fee is payable shall be of no effect unless the fee has been paid.

plain_english_summary: All design registration matters are fee-based, and a proceeding has no legal effect until the required fee is paid.

title: Notice of trust not to be entered in registers
text: There shall not be entered in any register kept under this Act, or be receivable by the Controller, any notice of any trust expressed, implied or constructive.
plain_english_summary: The Register of Designs only reflects legal ownership, not beneficial/trust arrangements — a nominee or trust structure behind a design owner won't appear on the public record.

title: Inspection of and extracts from registers
text: Every register kept under this Act shall at all convenient times be open to public inspection, subject to the provisions of this Act; certified copies of any entry, sealed with the Patent Office seal, shall be given to any person on payment of the prescribed fee.

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that where the register is maintained wholly or partly on computer, inspection shall be made by inspecting the computer print-out of the relevant entry.

plain_english_summary: The register is publicly inspectable, and certified copies of entries (including computer-maintained ones) can be obtained on payment of a fee.

title: Privilege of reports of Controller
text: Reports of or to the Controller made under this Act, other than the report referred to in section 45, shall not in any case be published or be open to public inspection.
plain_english_summary: Internal reports made to or by the Controller are confidential and not publicly disclosed (unlike the annual report to Parliament under section 45).

title: Prohibition of publication of drawings, etc. where application abandoned, etc.
text: Where an application for a design has been abandoned or refused, the application and any drawings, photographs, tracings, representations or specimens filed with it shall not at any time be open to public inspection or be published by the Controller.
plain_english_summary: If a design application is abandoned or refused, the design materials filed with it stay confidential forever and are never published — protects applicants whose registration attempt failed from having their design disclosed to competitors.

title: Power for Controller to correct clerical errors
text: The Controller may, on request in writing accompanied by the prescribed fee, correct any clerical error in the representation of a design or in the name or address of the proprietor, or in any other matter entered on the register of designs.
plain_english_summary: Clerical/typographical errors on the register (e.g. a misspelled proprietor name) can be corrected by the Controller on request.

title: Entry of assignments and transmissions in register
text: (1) A person who becomes entitled to the copyright in a registered design by assignment, transmission or other operation of law may apply to the Controller to register their title; the Controller, on proof to their satisfaction, registers them as proprietor and enters the assignment/transmission in the register.

sub_structure.2: (2) A person entitled as mortgagee, licensee or otherwise to an interest in a registered design may similarly apply to have that interest noted in the register.
sub_structure.3: (3) An assignment, mortgage, licence or creation of any other interest in a design is not valid unless in writing, reduced to an instrument covering all terms and conditions, and filed for registration with the Controller within six months of execution (extendable by a further six months on application).
sub_structure.4: (4) A registered proprietor has full power, subject to the Act and any registered rights of others, to assign, license or otherwise deal with the design and give valid receipts for consideration.
sub_structure.5: (5) Except for rectification applications under section 31, an unregistered assignment/instrument is not admissible in evidence in any court as proof of title, unless the court directs otherwise for recorded reasons.

plain_english_summary: Assignments and licences of a registered design must be in writing as a full instrument and filed with the Controller within six months of execution to be registered and legally effective — directly relevant to drafting design assignment/licence agreements, since an unregistered transfer generally cannot be proven in court.

title: Rectification of register
text: (1) The Controller may, on application by any aggrieved person, order the making, expunging or varying of an entry in the register of designs — covering non-insertion, wrongful entry, entries wrongly remaining, or errors/defects — and rectify the register accordingly.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Controller may decide any question necessary or expedient for the rectification.
sub_structure.3: (3) An appeal lies to the High Court from any Controller order under this section; the Controller may also refer an application directly to the High Court.
sub_structure.4: (4) An order of the Court rectifying the register must be served as notice on the Controller, who then rectifies the register.
sub_structure.5: (5) This section does not empower the Controller to cancel a registration — that is governed by section 19.

plain_english_summary: Provides a correction mechanism for the register itself (distinct from cancellation of the design under section 19), with a right of appeal to the High Court.

title: Powers of Controller in proceedings under Act
text: Subject to any rules, the Controller in any proceedings before him under this Act shall have the powers of a civil court for receiving evidence, administering oaths, enforcing attendance of witnesses, compelling discovery and production of documents, issuing commissions for examining witnesses, and awarding costs; such an award is executable as if it were a decree of that court.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Controller civil-court-equivalent powers when conducting proceedings, including the power to compel evidence and award enforceable costs.

title: Exercise of discretionary power by Controller
text: Where a discretionary power is given to the Controller under this Act, he shall not exercise it adversely to a design-registration applicant without giving the applicant an opportunity to be heard, if the applicant so requires within the prescribed time.
plain_english_summary: A natural-justice safeguard: the Controller cannot rule against an applicant on a discretionary matter without a hearing, if requested in time.

title: Power of Controller to take directions of the Central Government
text: The Controller may, in any case of doubt or difficulty arising in the administration of any provision of this Act, apply to the Central Government for directions in the matter.
plain_english_summary: The Controller can escalate unclear or difficult administrative questions to the Central Government for direction.

title: Refusal to register a design in certain cases
text: (1) The Controller may refuse to register a design whose use would, in his opinion, be contrary to public order or morality.

sub_structure.2: (2) An appeal lies to the High Court from an order of the Controller under this section.

plain_english_summary: The Controller retains a public-order/morality-based discretion to refuse registration, appealable to the High Court.

title: Appeals to the High Court
text: (1) Where an appeal is declared by this Act to lie from the Controller to the High Court, it must be made within three months of the date of the Controller's order.

sub_structure.2: (2) In calculating the three months, time spent obtaining a copy of the appealed order is excluded.
sub_structure.3: (3) The High Court may obtain expert assistance in deciding such appeals, and its decision is final.
sub_structure.4: (4) The High Court may make rules consistent with this Act governing the conduct and procedure of proceedings before it.

plain_english_summary: Sets a 3-month limitation period for appeals to the High Court from Controller decisions, and makes the High Court's decision final (no further statutory appeal).

title: Evidence before the Controller
text: Subject to any rules made under section 44, in any proceeding before the Controller, evidence shall be given by affidavit unless the Controller directs otherwise; the Controller may take oral (viva voce) evidence in lieu of or in addition to affidavit evidence, or allow cross-examination on an affidavit.
plain_english_summary: Proceedings before the Controller normally run on affidavit evidence, with discretion to allow oral testimony or cross-examination.

title: Certificate of Controller to be evidence
text: A certificate purporting to be under the hand of the Controller as to any entry, matter or thing which he is authorised by this Act or rules to make or do, shall be prima facie evidence of the entry having been made and of its contents, and of the matter or thing having been done or left undone.
plain_english_summary: A Controller-signed certificate is treated as prima facie proof of the facts it states, without needing further evidence.

title: Evidence of documents in Patent Office
text: Printed or written copies or extracts, certified by the Controller and sealed with the Patent Office seal, of documents in the Patent Office (and of registers and other books kept there) shall be admitted in evidence in all courts in India without further proof or production of the originals.

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that a court may, if it doubts the accuracy or authenticity of the copies, require production of the originals or further proof.

plain_english_summary: Certified copies of Patent Office records are self-authenticating in Indian courts, saving the need to produce originals, subject to a court's discretion to demand them if in doubt.

title: Applications and notices by post
text: Any application, notice or other document authorised or required to be left, made or given at the Patent Office or to the Controller, or to any other person under this Act, may be sent by post.
plain_english_summary: Filings and notices under the Act can be sent by post rather than delivered in person.

title: Declaration by infant, lunatic, etc.
text: (1) If a person is, by reason of infancy, lunacy or other disability, incapable of making a required statement or doing a required act under this Act, their lawful guardian, committee or manager (or a court-appointed person) may act or make the statement on their behalf.

sub_structure.2: (2) A court may make such an appointment on petition of a person acting on behalf of the disabled person, or any person interested in the statement/act being made.

plain_english_summary: Provides a mechanism for a guardian or court-appointed representative to act on behalf of a minor or legally incapacitated design applicant/proprietor.

title: Avoidance of certain restrictive conditions
text: (1) It is unlawful to insert, in a contract for sale/lease of an article bearing a registered design or in a licence to manufacture, use or package such an article, a condition that (a) requires or restricts the purchaser/lessee/licensee to acquire other articles only from the vendor/lessor/licensor or their nominees, or (b) prohibits or restricts them from using other articles not supplied by the vendor/lessor/licensor. Any such condition is void.

sub_structure.2: (2) Splitting such a condition into a separate agreement does not exempt it from this section.
sub_structure.3: (3) In a piracy proceeding under section 22, it is a defence to prove such an unlawful condition was in force in a contract relating to the design — unless the plaintiff is not a party to that contract and proves the condition was inserted without their knowledge/consent.
sub_structure.4: (4) This section does not: (a) affect a condition prohibiting sale of goods other than a particular person's; (b) validate an otherwise-invalid contract; or (c) affect a lease/licence condition reserving to the lessor/licensor the right to supply replacement parts or repair the article.
sub_structure.5: (5) This section also applies to pre-existing contracts if the unlawful restrictive condition continues in force beyond one year after commencement of this Act.

plain_english_summary: An anti-tying provision: design licences/sale contracts cannot lawfully force the buyer or licensee to exclusively source related goods from the design owner (or block them from using others' goods), subject to narrow carve-outs like spare-parts/repair rights. Directly relevant when drafting exclusivity or tying clauses in a design licensing agreement — such clauses risk being void.

title: Agents
text: (1) All applications and communications to the Controller under this Act may be signed by, and all attendances upon the Controller may be made by or through, a legal practitioner or an agent whose name and address is entered in the register of patent agents maintained under section 125 of the Patents Act, 1970.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Controller may, if he sees fit, require: (a) an agent to be resident in India; (b) a person not residing in India to employ an agent residing in India; or (c) the personal signature or presence of any applicant or other person.

plain_english_summary: Design applications can be filed through a lawyer or a registered patent agent; foreign applicants can be required to appoint an India-resident agent — relevant for startups working with overseas designers/founders.

title: Reciprocal arrangements with the United Kingdom and other convention countries or countries which are members of inter-governmental organisations
text: (1) A person who has applied for design protection in the United Kingdom or another convention country/group of countries/member of an inter-governmental organisation, or their legal representative/assignee, may claim priority for Indian registration dated to the earlier foreign application date, subject to conditions.

sub_structure.proviso_a: (a) the Indian application is made within six months of the first foreign application; and
sub_structure.proviso_b: (b) this does not entitle the proprietor to recover damages for piracy occurring before the design is actually registered in India.
sub_structure.2: (2) Registration in India is not invalidated merely because the design was exhibited, used, or its description published in India during the priority period.
sub_structure.3: (3) The convention application must otherwise follow the normal application process.
sub_structure.4: (4) The Central Government may, by notification, extend reciprocal protection to designs registered in a convention country where that country's law satisfactorily protects designs registered in India.

plain_english_summary: Implements the international priority right (akin to the Paris Convention) for designs: an applicant who first filed abroad has six months to claim the same priority date in India, without losing novelty due to interim disclosure in India.

title: Report of the Controller to be placed before Parliament
text: The Central Government shall cause to be placed before both Houses of Parliament once a year a report respecting the execution of this Act by or under the Controller.
plain_english_summary: Requires an annual report on the administration of the Act to be tabled in Parliament.

title: Protection of security of India
text: Notwithstanding anything in this Act, the Controller shall (a) not disclose any information relating to registration of a design or an application that he considers prejudicial to the security of India; and (b) take any action to cancel registration of designs that the Central Government, by notification, specifies as being in the interest of the security of India.

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation: 'security of India' means action necessary for security relating to a registered design's application to an article used for war or directly/indirectly for military establishments, war, or other international emergency.

plain_english_summary: National-security override: the Controller can withhold disclosure of, or cancel, designs connected to defence/military articles if the Central Government deems it necessary.

title: Power of Central Government to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.

sub_structure.2_examples: (2) Without prejudice to the generality of that power, rules may prescribe matters such as: application forms and fees (s.5(2)); registration timelines (s.5(5)); classification of articles (s.6(1)); manner of publication (s.7); restoration procedures and fees (ss.12-13); marking requirements (s.15); inspection fees (s.17); the form and fee for registering assignments/transmissions and rectification applications (ss.30-31); appeal fees (s.36); and any other matter required or permitted to be prescribed.
sub_structure.3: (3) Rule-making power under this section is subject to the rules being made after previous publication (i.e. draft rules must be published for comment).
sub_structure.4: (4) Every rule must be laid before both Houses of Parliament for 30 days, during which either House may modify or annul it, without prejudice to anything previously done under the rule.

plain_english_summary: Delegates detailed procedural rule-making (fees, forms, timelines) to the Central Government, subject to a public-comment requirement and Parliamentary oversight (a 30-day 'laying' period during which Parliament can modify or annul a rule).

title: Repeal and savings
text: (1) The Designs Act, 1911 is hereby repealed.

sub_structure.2: (2) Without prejudice to the General Clauses Act, 1897 as to repeals, anything done, issued or granted under the Designs Act, 1911 (notifications, rules, orders, registrations, certificates, notices, decisions, directions, approvals, authorisations, consents, applications, requests, etc.) that was in force at commencement of this Act continues in force as if made under the corresponding provisions of this Act.
sub_structure.3: (3) This Act applies to any pending design registration application at commencement, and to proceedings and registrations consequent thereon.
sub_structure.4: (4) Notwithstanding this Act, any court proceeding pending at commencement may continue as if this Act had not been passed.
sub_structure.5: (5) The date of expiration of copyright in designs registered before commencement is calculated under the old 5(+5)-year term structure that applied under the 1911 Act, not the new 10(+5)-year term.

plain_english_summary: Repeals the old Designs Act, 1911, but preserves everything already done under it (registrations, pending applications, court proceedings) and applies a transitional rule so that designs registered under the old Act keep their original 5(+5)-year term rather than getting the new Act's longer 10(+5)-year term retroactively.

title: Short title, extent and commencement
text: (1) This Act may be called the Trade Marks Act, 1999.

sub_structure.2: (2) It extends to the whole of India.
sub_structure.3: (3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.
sub_structure.proviso: Provided that different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Act, and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Act shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the official name of the Act, confirms it applies across all of India, and notes that different sections could be brought into force on different dates by government notification (the Act as a whole commenced on 15 September 2003).

title: Definitions and interpretation
text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,-

sub_structure.m: "mark" includes a device, brand, heading, label, ticket, name, signature, word, letter, numeral, shape of goods, packaging or combination of colours or any combination thereof;
sub_structure.r: "permitted use", in relation to a registered trade mark, means use of the trade mark by a registered user in relation to goods or services with which he is connected in the course of trade and for which he is registered as registered user, subject to any conditions or limitations to which that registration is subject; or use by a person other than the registered proprietor and registered user, with the written consent of the registered proprietor, subject to any conditions or limitations to which such consent is subject;
sub_structure.x: "registered user" means a person who is for the time being registered as such under section 49;
sub_structure.zb: "trade mark" means a mark capable of being represented graphically and which is capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of others and may include shape of goods, their packaging and combination of colours; and includes a certification trade mark or collective mark;
sub_structure.zg: "well known trade mark", in relation to any goods or services, means a mark which has become so well known to the substantial segment of the public which uses such goods or receives such services that the use of such mark in relation to other goods or services would be likely to be taken as indicating a connection in the course of trade between those goods or services and a person using the mark in relation to the first-mentioned goods or services.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Act's core vocabulary. Most important for a SaaS/software business: 'mark' covers names, logos, labels and packaging (which can include app icons and product names); 'trade mark' must be graphically representable and distinctive; and 'permitted use'/'registered user' are the statutory basis for trademark licensing - a business can only rely on a licensee's use of its mark to keep the mark alive if the licence is a registered-user arrangement or otherwise meets the 'permitted use' conditions.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Appointment of Registrar and other officers
text: (1) The Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint a person to be known as the Controller-General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, who shall be the Registrar of Trade Marks for the purposes of this Act.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Central Government may appoint such other officers with such designations as it thinks fit for the purpose of discharging, under the superintendence and direction of the Registrar, such functions of the Registrar under this Act as he may from time to time authorise them to discharge.

plain_english_summary: The same official who heads the Patents and Designs offices (the Controller-General) also serves as the Registrar of Trade Marks, who can delegate functions to other appointed officers.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Power of Registrar to withdraw or transfer cases, etc.
text: Without prejudice to the generality of the provisions of sub-section (2) of section 3, the Registrar may, by order in writing and for reasons to be recorded therein, withdraw any matter pending before an officer appointed under the said sub-section (2) and deal with such matter himself either de novo or from the stage it was so withdrawn or transfer the same to another officer so appointed.
plain_english_summary: Lets the Registrar pull a pending case away from a subordinate officer and either decide it personally or hand it to another officer, picking up from scratch or from where it left off.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Trade Marks Registry and offices thereof
text: (1) For the purposes of this Act, there shall be a trade marks registry and the Trade Marks Registry established under the Trade and Merchandise Marks Act, 1958 shall be the Trade Marks Registry under this Act.

sub_structure.2: (2) The head office of the Trade Marks Registry shall be at such place as the Central Government may specify, and branch offices may be established as the Central Government thinks fit.
sub_structure.4: (4) There shall be a seal of the Trade Marks Registry.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the Trade Marks Registry (carried over from the earlier 1958 Act) with a head office and branch offices, and its own official seal.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: The Register of Trade Marks
text: (1) For the purposes of this Act, a record called the Register of Trade Marks shall be kept at the head office of the Trade Marks Registry, wherein shall be entered all registered trade marks with the names, addresses and description of the proprietors, notifications of assignment and transmissions, the names, addresses and descriptions of registered users, conditions, limitations and such other matter relating to registered trade marks as may be prescribed.

sub_structure.2: (2) It shall be lawful for the Registrar to keep the records wholly or partly in computer floppies, diskettes or any other electronic form subject to such safeguards as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.4: (4) No notice of any trust, express or implied or constructive, shall be entered in the register and no such notice shall be receivable by the Registrar.

plain_english_summary: Creates the central Register of Trade Marks recording proprietors, assignments, and registered users (i.e. licensees) - which can be maintained electronically - and clarifies that ownership disputes involving trusts are outside its scope.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Classification of goods and services
text: (1) The Registrar shall classify goods and services, as far as may be, in accordance with the International classification of goods and services for the purposes of registration of trade marks.

sub_structure.2: (2) Any question arising as to the class within which any goods or services falls shall be determined by the Registrar whose decision shall be final.

plain_english_summary: Trade marks are registered against the international (NICE) classification of goods and services, and the Registrar has the final say on which class a given product or service falls into - relevant when a startup decides which classes (e.g. Class 9 software, Class 42 SaaS) to register its brand in.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Publication of alphabetical index
text: (1) The Registrar may publish in the prescribed manner an alphabetical index of classification of goods and services referred to in section 7.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where any goods or services are not specified in the alphabetical index published under sub-section (1), the classification shall be determined by the Registrar in accordance with sub-section (2) of section 7.

plain_english_summary: The Registrar may publish a searchable alphabetical index of how goods/services map onto the classification system, and decides the classification for anything not listed.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Absolute grounds for refusal of registration
text: (1) The trade marks- (a) which are devoid of any distinctive character, that is to say, not capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of another person; (b) which consist exclusively of marks or indications which may serve in trade to designate the kind, quality, quantity, intended purpose, values, geographical origin or the time of production of the goods or rendering of the service or other characteristics of the goods or service; (c) which consist exclusively of marks or indications which have become customary in the current language or in the bona fide and established practices of the trade, shall not be registered:

sub_structure.proviso: Provided that a trade mark shall not be refused registration if before the date of application for registration it has acquired a distinctive character as a result of the use made of it or is a well-known trade mark.
sub_structure.2: (2) A mark shall not be registered as a trade mark if it is of such nature as to deceive the public or cause confusion; contains matter likely to hurt religious susceptibilities; comprises scandalous or obscene matter; or its use is prohibited under the Emblems and Names (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950.
sub_structure.3: (3) A mark shall not be registered if it consists exclusively of the shape of goods resulting from the nature of the goods, the shape necessary to obtain a technical result, or the shape which gives substantial value to the goods.
sub_structure.explanation: Explanation.-For the purposes of this section, the nature of goods or services in relation to which the trade mark is used or proposed to be used shall not be a ground for refusal of registration.

plain_english_summary: Sets the core registrability bar: a mark (including a product or app name) cannot be registered if it is purely generic, merely descriptive of the goods/service, or has become a common trade term - unless it has acquired distinctiveness through use or is well-known. Software founders picking a purely descriptive product name (e.g. 'Cloud Storage') risk exactly this refusal.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Limitation as to colour
text: (1) A trade mark may be limited wholly or in part to any combination of colours and any such limitation shall be taken into consideration by the Registrar or the High Court, as the case may be, having to decide on the distinctive character of the trade mark.

sub_structure.2: (2) So far as a trade mark is registered without limitation of colour, it shall be deemed to be registered for all colours.

plain_english_summary: An applicant can register a mark limited to specific colours (relevant for brand colour palettes/logos), and a mark registered without any colour limitation is treated as covering all colours.

chapter_title: THE REGISTER AND CONDITIONS FOR REGISTRATION
title: Relative grounds for refusal of registration
